scope: Proposition 4.9 (Mass at a source-connected patch) of the manuscript “Buffered comparison and stopping-band resolution in critical Ising” (preprints/Buffered-comparison-and-stopping-band-resolution-in-critical-Ising-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d5167e3fe5fb85f4), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 17. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a > 0. Let b0 ⊆ z + Bw, and let L ⊆ z +Bw be a horizontal or vertical lattice segment of length at least aw and at most 2w. Suppose z + B16w is a free square-lattice neighborhood: it contains no common or disagreement pins. Then in the doubled model with arbitrary ordered pins outside this square, X x∈L P(x ←→ U) ≥ caw7/8 P(U ←→ b0). (4.18) The constant and lower threshold for w depend only on a. The same statement holds inside an isometric planar chart of a torus or cylinder.
